title: Battery Pass Consortium SAMM aspect models
authority: Battery Pass Consortium (published and validated via GEFEG)
usedFor: A conformance target for the battery product group — the sector with the earliest binding obligation date.
licence: CC-BY-4.0. Confirmed 2026-08-11 from the model files' own SPDX headers (`github.com/batterypass/BatteryPassDataModel`), not from the third-party survey — every `.ttl` file states `SPDX-License-Identifier: CC-BY-4.0`, copyright Circulor GmbH on behalf of the Battery Pass Consortium. The survey's `licence: null` was wrong; it never opened the source files.
source: https://github.com/batterypass/BatteryPassDataModel, main branch. Confirmed genuinely SAMM (files reference `urn:samm:org.eclipse.esmf.samm:meta-model:2.1.0` directly). Seven category models fetched: GeneralProductInformation, CarbonFootprint, Circularity, MaterialComposition, Performance (at 1.2.1, one minor ahead of the other six at 1.2.0), Labels, SupplyChainDueDiligence.
finding: This is NOT the SAMM vocabulary already recorded in this project. `dpp-aas` tracks `urn:samm:io.catenax.battery.battery_pass` — Catena-X / Eclipse Tractus-X — and this is `urn:samm:io.BatteryPass`, the Battery Pass Consortium's own. Two different aspect-model families under the same URN scheme, for the same product group, from two different organisations, confirmed still true after opening both. Field-by-field comparison against `BatteryData` (`crates/dpp-domain/src/domain/sector/data/battery.rs`) done 2026-08-11, category by category: GeneralProductInformation, CarbonFootprint, MaterialComposition, and Performance overlap heavily with what we already model (battery category, manufacturing date/place, mass, chemistry, rated capacity/energy/voltage, cycle counts, the Annex VII state-of-health parameter set). Circularity, Labels, and SupplyChainDueDiligence are almost entirely unmodelled on our side — batteryStatus, warrantyPeriod, pre-/post-consumer recycled-content split, hazardous-substance declarations (nothing analogous to `SvhcSubstance`, which electronics and textile both carry), spare-parts/end-of-life/collection information, and any conformity-declaration or label field are all absent from `BatteryData`. Performance also has fields we don't: min/max voltage, rated maximum power, capacity/power/round-trip-efficiency fade rates, and C-rate test conditions.
nextStep: This is a gap list, not a field-adoption list — none of the absent fields above may become an `Option` on `BatteryData` without its own citation to Annex VI/VII/XIII or another Battery Regulation article, per this project's own rule (a third party modelling a field is not a legal basis). Next: read Annex VI Part A/B and Annex XIII against each gap category above, starting with hazardous substances (Art. 9 already restricts Hg/Cd as rule thresholds but nothing declares them as a field) and the pre-/post-consumer recycled-content split (Annex II likely defines these terms precisely, unlike our current flat per-metal percentages).
